Both store their tables in Delta format in OneLake, so a data scientist can read warehouse tables from a Spark notebook. As a rule of thumb, choose the lakehouse for mixed or unstructured data, Spark code, data science and medallion pipelines, and choose the warehouse for a SQL-first team that needs T-SQL writes and multi-table transactions.

concepts.heading: Getting Data In: Pipelines, Mirroring, and Shortcuts
concepts.body: Fabric offers several ways to bring data into OneLake. Data Factory pipelines orchestrate copy, notebook and stored procedure steps on a schedule, and Dataflow Gen2 gives analysts low-code Power Query transformations. Mirroring continuously replicates an operational database, such as Azure SQL Database or Azure Cosmos DB, into OneLake as analytics-ready Delta tables in near real time, without anyone authoring or running ETL pipelines. Shortcuts give zero-copy access: a shortcut is a live reference that makes data stored elsewhere, such as in Azure Data Lake Storage, Amazon S3 or another OneLake location, appear inside a lakehouse while the data stays where it is. For example, a company whose files must stay in an Amazon S3 bucket for compliance can still query them in Fabric through a shortcut. On the exam, data must not be copied points to a shortcut, a near real-time copy of a database without pipelines points to mirroring, and scheduled multi-step work points to a pipeline.

concepts.heading: Medallion Layers and Direct Lake
concepts.body: Many Fabric and Databricks lakehouses organize data in the medallion architecture. The bronze layer holds raw data exactly as it arrived; the silver layer holds cleaned and validated data, with duplicates removed and formats standardized; and the gold layer holds curated, business-ready tables, often a star schema for reporting. Keep bronze unchanged, so that silver and gold can always be rebuilt if cleaning logic later turns out to be wrong. To report on gold tables, a Fabric semantic model can use Direct Lake mode, which loads data directly from the Delta tables in OneLake into memory without importing a separate copy into the model. That fits the one-copy idea of OneLake: there is no nightly copy of the gold tables into a separate model store. For example, a sales team's gold Delta tables feed a Direct Lake semantic model, and its Power BI reports read current data quickly without a scheduled import of the whole dataset.

concepts.heading: Azure Databricks
concepts.body: Azure Databricks is a cloud analytics platform built on Apache Spark for data engineering, data science, machine learning and SQL analytics. Unlike Fabric, it runs as a managed service inside your Azure subscription: it deploys and manages the cloud infrastructure for you, and it uses Delta Lake as its native table format. Spark processes huge data volumes quickly by splitting the data across the nodes of a cluster and processing the parts in parallel. Unity Catalog provides governance across a Databricks workspace: fine-grained access control on tables, data lineage, and discovery of data and AI assets. A Databricks SQL warehouse is the compute that runs many concurrent SQL and BI queries directly against lakehouse tables. Learn's reasons to choose Azure Databricks include a code-first Spark approach, existing Databricks skills, and portability because Databricks also runs on other clouds, while one unified SaaS workspace on OneLake points to Microsoft Fabric.

examPoints: A question that contrasts a read-only SQL analytics endpoint with full T-SQL writes and multi-table transactions is testing Fabric lakehouse versus Fabric warehouse.
A scenario that says data must stay where it is is testing OneLake shortcuts, while one that wants a near real-time replica of an operational database without pipelines is testing Fabric mirroring.

A question that compares delivery models is testing Microsoft Fabric as SaaS on OneLake versus Azure Databricks as a Spark-based managed service in your subscription, with Unity Catalog for its governance.

quiz.q: An analyst runs a T-SQL DELETE statement against a Fabric lakehouse through its SQL analytics endpoint, and it fails although SELECT queries work. The team needs T-SQL writes on these tables. What should it use?
choices: A Real-Time Intelligence eventhouse, which stores the same tables and accepts T-SQL write statements from analysts
A Fabric warehouse, which supports full T-SQL with inserts, updates, deletes and multi-table transactions
A OneLake shortcut, which turns the read-only lakehouse tables into writable tables for T-SQL statements
A Power BI semantic model in Direct Lake mode, which lets report users delete rows from the Delta tables
quiz.explain: The lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint is read-only, so T-SQL writes need a Fabric warehouse, which supports full T-SQL DML and multi-table transactions. Choice C is tempting because shortcuts link data into a lakehouse, but a shortcut only references data in place and does not change what the SQL analytics endpoint can do.

quiz.q: A company's data engineers write PySpark code, already use Databricks on another cloud and want the same platform on Azure, with central access control and lineage for their tables. What fits best?
choices: Microsoft Fabric Dataflow Gen2, with low-code Power Query steps and OneLake shortcuts to the other cloud
Azure Data Factory pipelines, with copy activities that move each table into Azure SQL Database every night
A Fabric warehouse, with T-SQL stored procedures that rewrite the PySpark jobs and manage table permissions
Azure Databricks, with Spark notebooks for the PySpark code and Unity Catalog for access control and lineage
quiz.explain: Code-first Spark, existing Databricks skills and multicloud portability are the reasons Learn gives for Azure Databricks, and Unity Catalog provides fine-grained access control and lineage. Choice A is tempting because Fabric is the other main analytics platform, but Dataflow Gen2 is a low-code tool, the opposite of the PySpark approach the engineers already use.

days.recap: Fabric is SaaS on OneLake with Data Factory, Data Engineering, Data Warehouse, Data Science, Real-Time Intelligence and Power BI; lakehouse for Spark and mixed data, warehouse for T-SQL writes; mirroring replicates databases, shortcuts avoid copies, Direct Lake reads Delta directly; Azure Databricks is managed Spark in your subscription with Unity Catalog.

days.title: Real-Time Analytics: Batch Versus Stream, Fabric Real-Time Intelligence, Event Hubs, and Stream Analytics

concepts.heading: Batch Versus Stream Processing
concepts.body: Batch processing collects data over a period and processes the whole group later, for example a credit card bill that lists a month of purchases or a nightly job that loads the day's orders into a warehouse. It can work on all the data at once, run complex analysis, and its results typically arrive hours later. Stream processing handles each event, or a small rolling window of recent events, as it arrives, with latency in seconds or milliseconds, and usually runs simpler aggregates such as counts, averages and thresholds. A fire alarm system that must sound alarms the moment sensors read high heat needs streaming, because waiting for a nightly batch would be useless. Many solutions combine both: they stream data to live dashboards and alerts and also persist it, so the same events can be analyzed in batch later. For example, a city shows cars per minute on a live dashboard and also studies a full year of traffic volumes.

concepts.heading: Event Sources and Azure Event Hubs
concepts.body: A general stream processing architecture has four parts: an event that generates data, such as a sensor reading or a click; a streaming source that captures the events; a perpetual query that runs continuously over the stream, filtering and aggregating it; and an output sink that receives the results, such as a database table, a file, a dashboard or another queue. On Azure, Azure Event Hubs is the fully managed service for ingesting very high volumes of events, such as GPS updates from thousands of vans or telemetry from apps, and it is the most common streaming source. Event Hubs also offers a Kafka endpoint, so existing Apache Kafka producers can send events to it, often with only a configuration change, and no Kafka cluster to run. Event Hubs Capture can automatically save every event to Azure Data Lake Storage or Blob Storage for later batch analysis. Azure IoT Hub is the matching source when the events come from IoT devices that also need to be managed.

concepts.heading: Azure Stream Analytics and Time Windows
concepts.body: Azure Stream Analytics is a fully managed stream processing service with no clusters to provision. A job has three parts: inputs, such as Event Hubs or IoT Hub; a query written in a SQL-like language; and outputs, such as Azure SQL Database, a data lake or Power BI. Because a stream never ends, its queries aggregate over temporal windows that give each result a start and an end. A tumbling window is a series of fixed-size, non-overlapping periods, so every event is counted exactly once, for example events per sensor for each minute. A hopping window has a fixed size but moves forward by a smaller step, so windows overlap and one event can appear in several results. A sliding window produces output only when an event enters or leaves the window. A session window groups events that arrive close together and closes after a period with no data. A snapshot window groups events that share the same timestamp.

concepts.heading: Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence
concepts.body: Real-Time Intelligence is the Fabric workload for ingesting, analyzing and acting on streaming data. An eventstream brings events into Fabric without code: you add sources such as Azure Event Hubs, Azure IoT Hub or Kafka, apply drag-and-drop transformations such as filter, aggregate and group by, and route results to destinations such as an eventhouse, a lakehouse or Activator. An eventhouse is the store for time-based event data: it holds one or more KQL databases, organizes data by arrival time, and lets analysts query billions of events in seconds with Kusto Query Language, for example Telemetry | where Timestamp > ago(1h) | summarize avg(Temperature) by DeviceId. Real-Time Dashboards show live visualizations. Activator watches data and takes actions without code when a condition is met, such as sending a Teams message when a freezer gets too warm. The Real-Time hub is the catalog where people discover, explore and share the data streams they can access across the organization.

concepts.heading: Spark Structured Streaming
concepts.body: Teams that already use Apache Spark for batch work can process streams with the same engine through Spark Structured Streaming. It treats a stream as an unbounded table that keeps receiving new rows, so engineers write the same DataFrame code they use for batch data, and Spark processes new rows continuously. Spark Structured Streaming runs in Spark environments such as Azure Databricks and Microsoft Fabric notebooks, and it can read from sources such as Azure Event Hubs or Kafka. A common pattern is to write the stream into a Delta Lake table: Delta's transactions protect against partial writes, and the same table can receive live events and serve batch queries over the full history. For example, a Databricks team that already cleans sales files with PySpark can add a streaming job that reads card transactions from Event Hubs and appends them to a Delta table that both a live alert job and a monthly report use.

examPoints: A scenario that must react within seconds, such as an alarm or a fraud alert, is testing stream processing, while one that processes a whole period at once, such as monthly bills, is testing batch processing.
A question that describes fixed, non-overlapping periods where each event counts once is testing a tumbling window, and overlapping fixed windows mean a hopping window.

A question about Fabric streaming is testing the Real-Time Intelligence parts: eventstream ingests and routes, eventhouse stores events for KQL queries, Activator acts on conditions, and Real-Time hub catalogs streams.

quiz.q: A Fabric team stores machine telemetry in an eventhouse. It wants an email sent to the maintenance lead automatically, without code, whenever any machine's vibration exceeds a limit. What should it use?
choices: A Real-Time Dashboard, which refreshes its tiles every few seconds so the maintenance lead can watch for high values
The Real-Time hub, which lists every stream in the organization and emails its owners when a new value arrives
Activator, which watches the data and sends an email or other action when a set condition is met
A KQL queryset, which runs a saved Kusto query on a schedule and stores the matching rows in a new table
quiz.explain: Activator is the Real-Time Intelligence item that watches data and automatically takes actions, such as an email or a Teams message, when a condition is met, without code. Choice A is tempting because a Real-Time Dashboard shows the values live, but it only visualizes data; someone would still have to watch it and act.

quiz.q: A streaming job must report the average temperature of the last ten minutes, recalculated every two minutes, so that each reading counts in several results. Which window type fits?
choices: A hopping window of ten minutes that moves forward by two minutes, so the windows overlap with each other
A tumbling window of ten minutes, so each reading is counted in exactly one of the fixed periods it falls in
A session window that groups readings arriving close together and closes after two minutes with no new data
A snapshot window that groups the readings sharing one timestamp and recalculates them every two minutes
quiz.explain: A hopping window has a fixed size, here ten minutes, and hops forward by a smaller step, here two minutes, so windows overlap and each reading appears in several results. Choice B is tempting because tumbling windows also have a fixed size, but they never overlap, so each reading would count only once and results would come only every ten minutes.

days.recap: Batch processes a whole period later, streaming handles events in seconds; Event Hubs and IoT Hub are the usual sources, Stream Analytics runs SQL-like queries over tumbling, hopping, sliding, session and snapshot windows, Fabric Real-Time Intelligence uses eventstreams, eventhouses with KQL, Activator and the Real-Time hub, and Spark Structured Streaming brings DataFrame code to streams.

days.title: Power BI: Tools, Reports and Dashboards, Data Models, and Visuals

concepts.heading: Power BI Desktop, Service, and Mobile
concepts.body: Power BI is Microsoft's tool set for data analytics and visualization, and the usual flow has three steps. You build in Power BI Desktop, a Windows application where you connect to sources such as Excel workbooks and SQL databases, clean and shape the data in Power Query Editor, define the data model, and design report pages. You then publish to the Power BI service, the cloud service where people open reports in a web browser, share them, build dashboards, and schedule refresh so the data updates without anyone opening the file. Finally, people consume reports, dashboards and apps in a browser or in the Power BI mobile app on phones and tablets, which is for viewing and interacting, not for building models. Content in the service lives in workspaces, where a team collaborates on its items. For example, an analyst builds a sales report in Desktop, publishes it, schedules a morning refresh, and managers read it on their phones.

concepts.heading: Reports, Dashboards, and Apps
concepts.body: A report is an interactive view, of one or more pages, of one semantic model. Its visuals are linked: selecting the Seattle bar in a sales by city chart filters or highlights related data in the other visuals on the page, and users can slice and filter freely. A dashboard is a single page of tiles that you pin from one or more reports, so it can bring together key figures from many sources in one place, and data alerts on card, gauge and KPI tiles can email people when a number crosses a threshold. Dashboards are created in the Power BI service, not in Desktop. An app packages a set of finished reports and dashboards from a workspace and publishes them to a wide audience, with permissions separate from those of the workspace. For example, a finance team can publish one app with four reports and two dashboards for two thousand employees, while only the team members can edit the workspace.

concepts.heading: Fact and Dimension Tables in a Star Schema
concepts.body: A semantic model is easiest to use when it follows dimensional modeling. Fact tables record events, such as each sale, with numeric measures such as quantity and revenue, and they usually have many rows. Dimension tables describe the entities you group and filter by, such as product, customer, store and date, with one row per entity, a unique key, and descriptive attributes such as name, city or category. In a star schema the fact table sits in the middle and each dimension relates directly to it. When a dimension branches into further detail tables, such as Product related to a separate Category table, the design is a snowflake schema. Relationships connect the tables: the key repeats in the fact table and is unique in the dimension, so Sales to Product is many-to-one, with the dimension on the one side. A hierarchy in a dimension, such as year, quarter, month and day in the Date table, lets users drill down from totals to detail.

concepts.heading: Measures, Calculated Columns, and Storage Modes
concepts.body: Measures and calculated columns are both written in DAX, but they behave differently. A measure is an aggregation, such as total revenue or average order value, evaluated at query time in the current filter context, so the same measure shows the right total for each year, region or product in a visual; it is not stored row by row. A calculated column computes a new value for each row, such as combining City and State into one field, and is stored in the table when the data refreshes, so it can be used in slicers, rows or axes. Models also have a storage mode. Import loads the data into the model's in-memory cache, which is fast and is Learn's default recommendation but shows changes only after a refresh. DirectQuery imports no data and sends queries to the source for each visual, for when data must stay in the source. Direct Lake, in Microsoft Fabric, reads Delta tables in OneLake directly without an imported copy.

concepts.heading: Choosing the Right Visual
concepts.body: The exam often describes a need and asks which visual fits. A card shows one important number, such as this year's revenue, that people read at a glance. A table lists related values in rows and columns, while a matrix groups data by rows and columns like a pivot table, with subtotals and drill-down, for example revenue by category and year. Bar and column charts compare values across discrete categories, such as sales for twelve product categories. A line chart shows a trend over time, such as monthly visits over three years. A pie or donut chart shows the share of a total for a small number of categories, such as four advertising channels. A scatter chart shows the relationship between two numeric measures, such as store size and revenue, with one point per item. A map compares values across geographic locations, such as late deliveries by region. When several visuals sit on one report page, they filter each other when a user selects a value.

examPoints: A question that asks where models are built, where content is shared and refreshed, and where people only view it is testing Power BI Desktop versus the Power BI service versus the mobile app.

A question that contrasts one page of tiles from many reports with alerts against a multi-page, interactive view of one model is testing dashboards versus reports, and distributing finished content widely points to an app.

A question that describes a new per-row value versus an aggregation that changes with filters is testing calculated columns versus measures, and data that must stay in the source points to DirectQuery.

quiz.q: A Power BI model has an Orders fact table with columns Quantity and UnitPrice. The author wants a Total Revenue value that adds up correctly by year, region or product in any visual. What should the author create?
choices: A calculated column that multiplies Quantity by UnitPrice and stores the result once for every single order row
A hierarchy in the Orders table that groups Quantity and UnitPrice so the visual can drill down to each order
A new dimension table that holds one row per revenue amount and relates many-to-one to the Orders fact table
A measure written in DAX that sums Quantity times UnitPrice and is evaluated in the filters of each visual
quiz.explain: A measure is a DAX aggregation evaluated at query time in the current filter context, so one Total Revenue measure gives the right total for any year, region or product a visual shows. Choice A is tempting because a calculated column can compute revenue per row, but it only stores a per-row value; the reusable aggregation that responds to filters is a measure.

quiz.q: An operations manager wants a visual that shows how the number of support tickets has risen or fallen each week over the last two years. Which visual should the report author choose?
choices: A pie chart, which shows what share of all support tickets over the two years falls into each individual week
A line chart, which shows how the weekly number of support tickets changes over the two years as a trend
A card, which shows the total number of support tickets over the two years as one large number at a glance
A scatter chart, which shows how the number of support tickets relates to a second numeric measure per week
quiz.explain: A line chart is the standard visual for a trend over time, such as weekly ticket counts over two years. Choice D is tempting because a scatter chart also plots points, but it is meant to show the relationship between two numeric measures, not how one value changes over time.

days.recap: Build in Power BI Desktop, publish and refresh in the service, view in a browser or mobile app; reports are multi-page views of one model, dashboards are one page of pinned tiles with alerts, apps distribute both; model facts and dimensions as a star schema with many-to-one relationships, hierarchies, measures and calculated columns; pick Import, DirectQuery or Direct Lake and match each need to a visual.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Commonly Confused Pairs, and Test-Day Plan

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: DP-900 gives you 45 minutes for the assessment, and you pass with a scaled score of 700 or greater. Microsoft does not publish the number of questions, so plan your pace by time rather than by a fixed count. The four domains are Describe core data concepts at 25 to 30 percent, Identify considerations for relational data on Azure at 20 to 25 percent, Describe considerations for working with non-relational data on Azure at 15 to 20 percent, and Describe an analytics workload at 25 to 30 percent. Questions describe and choose rather than configure, so focus on what each kind of data, service and tool is for, and on current names such as Microsoft Fabric, OneLake and Azure Data Lake Storage.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Data Concepts and Relational Data
concepts.body: Several early-domain mistakes come from look-alike pairs. Structured data fits a fixed schema of rows and columns, semi-structured data such as JSON carries its own flexible structure, and unstructured data such as images and video has none. Transactional workloads (OLTP) handle many small reads and writes with ACID guarantees, while analytical workloads (OLAP) read large volumes of historical data for reporting. A database administrator manages and secures databases, a data engineer builds pipelines and stores, and a data analyst models and visualizes data. A primary key uniquely identifies a row, while a foreign key points to a primary key in another table. Normalization splits data into related tables to reduce duplication. DDL statements such as CREATE and ALTER define objects, while DML statements such as INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE change rows. Azure SQL Database is fully managed for new cloud apps, SQL Managed Instance offers near-complete SQL Server compatibility, and SQL Server on Azure VMs gives full operating system control.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Non-Relational Data and Analytics
concepts.body: Later domains have their own pairs. Blob Storage holds unstructured objects, Azure Files holds shares that clients map, and Table storage holds key-attribute entities; Table storage is the cheap single-region option, while Azure Cosmos DB for Table adds global distribution and automatic indexes. Cool, cold and archive all lower storage cost, but only archive is offline and needs rehydration. Strong consistency always returns the latest write, while Session guarantees only that a client reads its own writes. ETL transforms before loading, while ELT loads first and transforms in the target. A Fabric lakehouse suits Spark and mixed data and its SQL analytics endpoint is read-only, while a Fabric warehouse supports full T-SQL writes. Shortcuts reference data in place, while mirroring replicates a database into OneLake. Tumbling windows never overlap, while hopping windows do. A report is one or more interactive pages over one model, while a dashboard is one page of tiles. Import copies data into the model, while DirectQuery leaves it in the source.

concepts.heading: Use an Error Log
concepts.body: For every practice question you miss or guess, write down the pair of ideas you confused, such as cool versus archive tier, Session versus Strong consistency, or measure versus calculated column, and the clue in the stem that should have decided it. Reviewing these pairs is faster than rereading every day, because the same confusions tend to repeat. Spend the most time on the two largest domains, core data concepts and analytics workloads, unless your log shows a clear weak spot elsewhere. Read each scenario for its deciding phrase, such as must be readable at once, users around the world, data must not be copied, without writing code, or each event counted once, before looking at the choices, then eliminate choices that solve a different problem. Also watch for retired or outdated options in distractors: Azure Database for MariaDB is retired, and Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is on a retirement path, so neither is a good answer for a new solution.

concepts.heading: Test-Day Plan and Retake Policy
concepts.body: Arrive early or, for an online exam, check your room, webcam and system well before the start time. Read the instructions at the start of the exam and of each section carefully, because they explain how each question works and whether you can return to questions later. Make a first pass answering what you know and mark uncertain questions for review where review is allowed. With 45 minutes and an unpublished question count, check the timer now and then rather than spending long on one item. For multi-answer questions, choose exactly the number of answers requested. There is no penalty for guessing, so make sure every question has an answer before you finish. If you do not pass, Microsoft's retake policy for fundamentals exams says you wait 24 hours before the second attempt and 14 days between later attempts, with at most five attempts in 12 months from the first.

examPoints: A question that lists Blob Storage, Azure Files, Table storage and Azure Cosmos DB as choices is testing whether you can match unstructured objects, mapped shares, cheap key-attribute data and globally distributed NoSQL apart.

A question that lists pipelines, mirroring and shortcuts, or lakehouse and warehouse, is testing the Fabric pairs: scheduled multi-step work versus database replication versus zero-copy access, and Spark-first versus T-SQL writes.
A question that describes a reporting need is testing the Power BI pairs report versus dashboard, measure versus calculated column, and Import versus DirectQuery versus Direct Lake.

quiz.q: A learner keeps mixing up two Microsoft Fabric features for bringing data into OneLake. Which statement correctly separates mirroring from shortcuts?
choices: Mirroring replicates an operational database into OneLake, while a shortcut references data in place without copying it
Mirroring references external files in place without copying them, while a shortcut replicates a database into OneLake
Mirroring and shortcuts both copy data into OneLake on a schedule, but only shortcuts can transform it on the way in
Mirroring works only with Amazon S3 buckets, while a shortcut works only with databases such as Azure SQL Database
quiz.explain: Mirroring continuously replicates operational databases such as Azure SQL Database or Azure Cosmos DB into OneLake as Delta tables, while a shortcut is a live, zero-copy reference to data that stays where it is. Choice B is tempting because it names both real behaviors, but it swaps them between the two features.

quiz.q: A company keeps device settings in Azure Table storage in one region. It now needs the data in several regions with indexes on every property and minimal code changes. Which option fits?
choices: Azure Files, by moving each table into an SMB share that every region can map with the same paths
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, by rewriting the app to store each entity as a JSON document in a container
